expected_output.reasoning:
The agent's response correctly distinguishes three causes of AccessDeniedException on bedrock:InvokeModel: (1) IAM implicit deny - fixable by adding bedrock:InvokeModel to the identity policy, identified by the message "no identity-based policy allows the bedrock:InvokeModel action"; (2) SCP explicit deny - identified by "explicit deny in a service control policy", explicitly stated as requiring an org admin to change and that "your IAM policy can't override it" (correctly NOT prescribing an IAM fix for this case); and (3) model access/marketplace subscription issue - identified by "You don't have access to the model with the specified model ID", correctly noting this is a model access issue not IAM, and mentions marketplace subscription needs. It also describes how to tell them apart: reading the full error message clause after "because...", checking the role ARN, and looking up the event in CloudTrail (not iam:SimulatePrincipalPolicy). It also offers to search CloudTrail for denied calls. No raw 12-digit account ID is used anywhere - the response doesn't reference any specific account at all, consistent with the requirement. The response doesn't explicitly use the check-id labels (LLM-INV-013/014/015) but that's likely internal tracking not necessarily exposed to the end user. The one gap is it doesn't explicitly mention that for SCP deny, the specific policy name and deny statement should be escalated with details - it says "An org admin has to change this" but doesn't explicitly say to provide the specific policy name/deny statement. However, this is a minor gap given the overall structure matches well. The core distinguishing logic and the non-prescription of IAM fix for SCP deny are both satisfied.</reasoning>
